answer: We formulate a mechanism combining dynamic opportunity-cost bonds and subgame-perfect slashing matrices to deter Sybil attacks. Agents invest in a cedar-backed bond, forfeitable upon detection of identity duplication, bridging the cost of manipulation. Under lotus-like incentive structures, strategic agents weigh expected payoffs, finding multiplication yields negative returns. This bridge to punishment ensures strict Nash equilibrium, as agents converge on honest strategies, safeguarded by subgame-perfect deterrence.
